name: reaction-diffusion
title: Reaction-diffusion: bigraph coupling (headline)
question:
Do two independently-authored processes -- `DiffusionProcess` (no
knowledge of reactions) and `LogisticReactionProcess` (no knowledge of
FEM/diffusion) -- produce genuine Fisher-KPP reaction-diffusion dynamics
when wired to the same bigraph stores, with neither process calling into
the other?
hypothesis:
Coupling is entirely a property of the document wiring (shared
`stores.solution` / `stores.source` paths), not of either process's
implementation: with the reaction term active (r=2.0), the field's total
mass should grow dramatically faster than a near-zero-reaction control
(r=1e-9, identical wiring) run for the same duration, while logistic
saturation keeps the field bounded near the carrying capacity K.
objective:
Run the `reaction_diffusion` composite (DiffusionProcess ⊕
LogisticReactionProcess) and confirm (a) mass grows far faster than a
near-zero-reaction control under identical wiring/duration -- isolating
the reaction term's causal contribution from solver noise -- and (b) the
field stays bounded near the logistic carrying capacity K rather than
blowing up, which would indicate the `source` store were composing
additively instead of being overwritten each tick.
description:
This is the investigation's composability showcase. `DiffusionProcess`
(Task 3) and `LogisticReactionProcess` (Task 4) are coupled PURELY through
shared stores: `stores.solution` is read+written by `DiffusionProcess` and
read by `LogisticReactionProcess`; `stores.source` is written by
`LogisticReactionProcess` (`overwrite[array[float]]` -- a fresh per-tick
rate, not an accumulated delta) and read by `DiffusionProcess`, which
multiplies it by dt internally. Swap `LogisticReactionProcess` for any
other process that reads "solution" and writes "source" and
`DiffusionProcess` is none the wiser -- that substitutability is the
claim this study exists to demonstrate, du/dt = D*laplacian(u) +
r*u*(1-u/K) emerging from composition, not from either process
implementing Fisher-KPP itself.

expected_behavior.name: mass-grows-via-coupling
expected_behavior.en: Mass growth with the reaction coupled in (r=2.0) is at least 5x growth under a near-zero-reaction control (r=1e-9), same wiring/duration.
expected_behavior.rationale: A bare "mass increases" check is not discriminating -- solver/quadrature noise alone moves the integral by a small amount even with the reaction effectively disconnected (r~=0). Comparing against a near-zero-reaction control with IDENTICAL wiring isolates the reaction term's causal contribution, proving the growth comes from the composed coupling.

expected_behavior.name: field-bounded-by-k
expected_behavior.en: The field's maximum stays below 1.2 (K=1.0 plus margin) throughout the run.
expected_behavior.condition: max(solution) < 1.2 over the run (K=1.0 default carrying capacity)
expected_behavior.rationale: Logistic saturation (`r*u*(1-u/K)`) should cap growth near K regardless of run length. An unbounded field would indicate `stores.source` is composing additively across ticks instead of being overwritten each tick (the accumulate-vs-overwrite bug class this wiring is designed to avoid).

behavior_tests.name: mass-grows-via-coupling
behavior_tests.description:
(last_integral - first_integral) for the r=2.0 run must be at least 5x
the same quantity for a same-duration, same-wiring r=1e-9 control.

provenance.note: 5x is a clear-separation band between genuine reaction-driven growth and residual solver/quadrature noise, calibrated against the r~=0 control (observed ratio ~2.6e9x at r=2.0 vs r=1e-9, D=0.05, resolution=24, run_time=0.5).

behavior_tests.name: field-bounded-by-k
behavior_tests.description:
max(solution) across every recorded tick of the r=2.0 run must stay
below 1.2 (K=1.0 plus margin).

provenance.note: Logistic saturation caps u at K=1.0 in the continuous limit regardless of run length; 1.2 leaves headroom for discretization overshoot while still catching an accumulate-vs-overwrite regression, which blows well past this bound.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
No further studies in this investigation depend on reaction-diffusion --
it is the investigation's headline/terminal study, demonstrating the
composability claim the other three studies build up to.

canonical_runs.label: Fisher-KPP coupling (resolution=24, D=0.05, r=2.0 vs r=1e-9 control)
